claims.head: Martone gets company tonight
claims.call: The Capitals’ L2 (Protas, Dubois and Wilson) spends at least 52% of its 5-on-5 time against the Flyers’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Capitals keep sending Wilson’s line (Protas, Dubois and Wilson) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Spencer Carbery has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Flyers’ first line is Martone, Cates and Michkov.

claims.gist: At home, Spencer Carbery likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Flyers’ first line.

claims.head: The Capitals hunt better looks than the Flyers
claims.body: The Capitals wait for good looks, but the Flyers settle for hopeful ones. Washington is the league’s best for shot quality, and Philadelphia is near the bottom. The more dangerous chances should be the Capitals’.

WSH.head: The matchup suits the Capitals
WSH.body: Even though Washington will be without Dubois, Philadelphia is on the second night of a back-to-back, and the Capitals have been out-chancing opponents lately and have home-ice advantage. The Flyers’ way back in is a power play that gets going.

PHI.head: The Flyers face a real test
